title: George H.W. Bush as CIA director told of a UAP event and refused the film
summary: Eric Davis tells of George H.W. Bush as CIA director told of a UAP event and refused the film, about 1976 (event early 1960s) at The Pentagon, Arlington, Virginia, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he started rattling off about a major U UAP event um that was took place in early 60s and Bush's eyes lit up and this is what he's told me he said what are you talking about
As head of the CIA, he was made aware of it accidentally
tellings.difference: Identifies the event as the Holloman footage, says Bush learned of it accidentally, and is told by Michels secondhand rather than by Davis.
tellings.link_reason: Both say George H.W. Bush, as CIA director, was told of an early-1960s UAP event and its film, relayed through Eric Davis.

as_told.title: George H.W. Bush made aware of the Holloman footage

tellings.quote: So he goes into this for his first briefing as director of the CIA. The first thing that came out of this briefer's mouth was the Hollowman landing in April 1964 at Hollowman uh Air Force Base in New Mexico. So he started briefing Bush on that and Bush said, "What are you talking about? I've never heard of this before."
tellings.difference: Names the event as the April 1964 Holloman AFB landing and places it in his first briefing, without the film refusal.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell Bush as new CIA director being briefed on an early-1960s UAP event and reacting with surprise.

as_told.title: George H.W. Bush's first CIA briefing on the Holloman landing

plain: Eric Davis, a scientist who has worked on Pentagon studies, says that George H.W. Bush, in his first briefing as head of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, in 1976, heard a briefer describe a major event involving unexplained objects from the early 1960s, and asked what on earth they were talking about, having never heard of it. In one telling Davis names the event as a landing at Holloman Air Force Base in New Mexico in April 1964, and in the story's earliest form Bush also refused to look at film of it, while the podcast host Jesse Michels later retells it as Bush learning of the event by accident. If true, it would mean even the CIA's own director had been kept in the dark.
